counterfactual_missing_items: No evidence of pulmonary embolism or pulmonary arteriovenous fistulae
Pulmonary artery pressure was 60/39 mmHg, lower than aortic pressure
decisive_items: The patient was initially acyanotic from 2010 to 2016, but gradually became cyanotic after an episode of severe cough and hemoptysis
Revealed a patent foramen ovale measuring 7.34 mm in width with a continuous, pure right-to-left shunt on colour flow mapping
Markedly enlarged right atrium and right ventricle, with tricuspid regurgitation
response.rationale: R6 integrates the full clinical picture: chronic cyanosis, right-to-left shunt through a PFO, pulmonary hypertension, and right heart enlargement, matching Eisenmenger syndrome. R7 only identifies the PFO without explaining the cyanosis and pulmonary hypertension. R5 and R3 are partial findings subsumed by R6. R4 is contradicted by the absence of pulmonary embolism on angiography.

rejected.why: Directly contradicted by pulmonary angiography showing no evidence of pulmonary embolism or arteriovenous fistulae, and hemoptysis is non-specific.
Only captures elevated pulmonary pressures, missing the right-to-left shunt and cyanosis that are essential for the diagnosis.
Tricuspid regurgitation is a secondary finding, not the underlying cause of the patient's presentation.
